issue.body:
<!-- For feature requests, just clear out the below 
Try to provide [a minimal, complete, and verifiable example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/mcve), preferably a [gist](https://gist.github.com/lbargaoanu/9c7233441c3a3413cc2b9b9ebb5964a9) that we can execute and see fail. [Here](https://gist.github.com/lbargaoanu/0cbc531306223f7ffc5468becf2642d6) is an example for ProjectTo.
-->

### Source/destination types

```csharp
public class Course
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
}

public class CourseModel
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
}
```

### Mapping configuration

```csharp
Mapper.Initialize(cfg =>
{
    cfg.CreateMap<Course, CourseModel>();
}); 
```

### Version: 6.0.2 - 6.1.1
<!-- Include the major/minor version (4.2.1, 5.2.0, 6.0.2 etc) --> 

### Expected behavior

<!-- What did you expect to happen? Or what used to happen in an older version? -->
Expression should be mapped without any errors.

### Actual behavior

<!-- What happened instead? -->
```
Unhandled Exception: System.NullReferenceException: Object reference not set to an instance of an object.
   at AutoMapper.XpressionMapper.XpressionMapperVisitor.FindDestinationFullName(Type typeSource, Type typeDestination, String sourceFullName, List`1 propertyMapInfoList)
   at AutoMapper.XpressionMapper.XpressionMapperVisitor.VisitMember(MemberExpression node)
   at System.Linq.Expressions.MemberExpression.Accept(ExpressionVisitor visitor)
   at System.Linq.Expressions.ExpressionVisitor.Visit(Expression node)
   at AutoMapper.XpressionMapper.XpressionMapperVisitor.VisitBinary(BinaryExpression node)
   at System.Linq.Expressions.BinaryExpression.Accept(ExpressionVisitor visitor)
   at System.Linq.Expressions.ExpressionVisitor.Visit(Expression node)
   at AutoMapper.XpressionMapper.Extensions.MapperExtensions.MapExpression[TDestDelegate](IMapper mapper, LambdaExpression expression)
   at AutoMapper.MapExpression.Issue.Program.Main(String[] args) in ...\AutoMapper.MapExpression.Issue\Program.cs:line 18
```
After investigation I figured out that the reason of NullReference was lack of configuration for mapping CourseModel to Course. After map creation, expression was mapped.
I think AutoMapperMappingException with details of missed mapping types will be more appropriate in this case. In addition, I was surprised why AutoMapper needed reverse mapping.

### Steps to reproduce

```csharp
Expression<Func<Course, bool>> exp = course => course.Id == 1;
var mappedExpresion = Mapper.Instance.MapExpression<Expression<Func<CourseModel, bool>>>(exp);
```
[Program.zip](https://github.com/AutoMapper/AutoMapper/files/1215552/Program.zip)

    }

    public class DestinationBase
    {
        public int IgnoreMe { get; private set; }
    }

### Mapping configuration

```csharp
var config = new MapperConfiguration(cfg =>
            {
                cfg.CreateMap<Source, Destination>()
                    .IgnoreAllPropertiesWithAnInaccessibleSetter();
            });
```

### Version: 5.0.2 - 7.0.1

### Expected behavior

The `IgnoreMe` member of the `Destination` object should be ignored when mapping.

### Actual behavior

The `IgnoreMe` member of the `Destination` object is *not* ignored and mapped without issues.

### Steps to reproduce

https://gist.github.com/JoesGab/48f136622234c9ef0ab6f26eb164d449

Note the `DestinationBase`! The test only fails in this case, passes if you put the `IgnoreMe` in the derived type.

The generic collection types also implement readonly versions of themselves.

issue.title: Dynamic ProjectTo
issue.body:
Unlike, `Map`, `ProjectTo` doesn't have a non-generic version:
```cs
IQueryable ProjectTo(IQueryable source, Type target, ...);
```

It's an edge case but it is useful when writing dynamic code.

issue.title: Consider trimming keys when mapping from dictionaries
Missing Method Exception (Parameterless Constructor) on ProjectTo()
Extensions API
issue.body:
# Problem description

When building extensions based on AutoMapper (AM) it does not exists any place where the configuration data can be stored together with the AM configuration. In AutoMapper.Collection (AMC) we are using static parameters to store the configured comparer that are configured together with the AM mapping. When running AM with AMC configuration in parallel; example for testing, the configuration will often be corrupt and mapping will not work correctly that will result in errors in the application. 

# Suggested solution

To be able to build stable extension on AM without all the time extend AM with new features I suggest to implement `FeatureCollection` that can handle all different possibilities extensions. The concept of `FeatureCollection` will be the same in AM as ASP.NET Core Http Abstraction is using to extend the Http Request with new features without need to change the core implementation.

A `FeatureCollection` is a typed dictionary where each item can be sealed when the configuration executes the `Seal`. The item in the `FeatureCollection` can be accessed during runtime and will act as the configuration store for the extensions.

In AM two places is identified that need the `FeatureCollection` that contains `IFeature`.

1. `IConfigurationProvider` (breaking change).
2. `TypeMap`.

To be able to populate the above `FeatureCollection`s the following members have been modified. The below `I*Feature` is used to configure the `IFeature` and place them in either the `IConfigurationProvider` or in the `TypeMap` before they are sealed.

1. `AdvancedConfiguration` to hold a collection of `IMapperConfigurationExpressionFeature` (this may be moved into `IMapperConfigurationExpression` for consistency).
2. `IMappingExpression` to hold a collection of `IMappingExpressionFeature` (breaking change).

See the linked PRs for proof of concept.

issue.title: Parameterized projections do not parameterize the query
AllowNullCollections=false not honored for ICollection
issue.body:
<!-- For feature requests, just clear out the below -->

### Source/destination types

```csharp
    public class Foo
    {
        public List<int> fooList = null;
    }

    public class FooDB
    {
        public ICollection<int> fooList = null;
    }
```

### Mapping configuration

```csharp
   public class ExplicitGlobalDefaultProfile : Profile
    {
        public ExplicitGlobalDefaultProfile()
        {
            AllowNullCollections = false;
            AllowNullDestinationValues = true;
            CreateMap<Foo, FooDB>();
        }
    }

    public class ImplicitGlobalDefaultProfile : Profile {
        public ImplicitGlobalDefaultProfile()
        {
            CreateMap<Foo, FooDB>();
        }
    }
```

### Version: x.y.z
6.1.0
### Expected behavior

I expect fooDB.fooList to be an empty collection of some kind.
In 6.0.2 (and 5.2.0) this is the actual behaviour.

### Actual behavior

fooList is null.

### Steps to reproduce

```csharp
        var explicitGlobalConfig = new MapperConfiguration(cfg => { cfg.AddProfile<ExplicitGlobalDefaultProfile>(); });
        var implicitGlobalConfig = new MapperConfiguration(cfg => { cfg.AddProfile<ImplicitGlobalDefaultProfile>(); });
        var explicitMapper = explicitGlobalConfig.CreateMapper();
        var implicitMapper = implicitGlobalConfig.CreateMapper();
        var foo = new Foo();
        var explicitFooDB = explicitMapper.Map<Foo, FooDB>(foo);
        var implicitFooDB = implicitMapper.Map<Foo, FooDB>(foo);
```
